title: Network worker/coordinator review fixes (queue refresh, record fields, URL parity)
summary: Fixes integration seams found in the Network Worker/Coordinator review that the unit suite stubbed over: the coordinator now re-scans the source queue so newly added media is distributed instead of only the start-time snapshot; claim metadata reads the real QueueRecord fields (is_priority/size_gb) with back-compat fallback; the worker coordinator URL is validated consistently across the dry-run precondition and the dispatcher (port required, bind-all rejected); and a stop whose provider ran but whose command-journal write failed now commits the stopped state instead of leaving a phantom running.
reason: 259/259 network unit tests passed while the live feature stalled because fixtures used SimpleNamespace records with priority/estimated_size_gb names and patched out the real dispatcher. Real QueueRecord exposes is_priority/size_gb, so every live claim reported priority=False and size 0.0; the coordinator queue was a one-shot snapshot loaded at start; the dry-run worker-URL precondition allowed a port-less URL the dispatcher then rejected, and the dispatcher validator did not reject 0.0.0.0; a stop whose journal write failed left lifecycle state showing running, blocking later starts.
behavior_before: Coordinator served only the queue records present when it started (no rescan); network claims always reported priority=False and estimated_size_gb=0.0 against real QueueRecord; a port-less worker coordinator URL passed dry-run preconditions but failed at provider startup; validate_coordinator_url accepted http://0.0.0.0:7830 (including the hot-swap path); a confirmed stop with a failing journal write left lifecycle state as running.
behavior_after: A daemon coordinator queue refresher re-scans build_queue_preview (force_refresh) on an interval (CoordinatorQueueRefreshSecs, default 15s, min 5s) and atomically swaps queue_records under a new app queue lock shared with the claim scan and queue removal; claim priority/size read is_priority/size_gb with fallback to the legacy names; the dry-run precondition requires a coordinator port to match the dispatcher; validate_coordinator_url rejects 0.0.0.0 and ::; a stop whose provider ran but journal failed commits the stopped state with cleanup_result=command_journal_failed_stop_state_committed.
manual_validation: unittest discover tests/python/desktop test_network*.py - passed (265 tests)
unittest tests.python.desktop.test_application_facade_process_launch test_application_facade_network test_api_contract_payload test_api_command_contracts - passed (69 tests)
operator_validation_required: AGENTS.md section 7 NOT self-certified (queue claim/launch + command journal adjacency). Run a real two-machine LAN pass: coordinator start, worker start with http://<coordinator-LAN-IP>:7830, confirm a claim/heartbeat/done cycle in cluster.log.
Add new media after the coordinator is running and confirm it gets distributed (validates the queue refresher).
Confirm priority files claim with priority and Worker Board shows non-zero GB.
Restart the running API/app so the rebuilt Python is loaded before testing.
rollback_plan: Revert coordinator_url.py, lifecycle_facade.py, coordinator_queue.py, coordinator_http_handlers.py, and network_lifecycle_provider.py to their prior revisions, delete tests/python/desktop/test_network_lifecycle_fixes.py, revert the test_network_security.py addition, then rerun the network, lifecycle, and dependency-boundary validations.
notes: Follow-up to MP-CHANGE-2026-0613-020. The queue refresher uses an unregistered optional config key CoordinatorQueueRefreshSecs (read defensively, not yet in the settings schema/UI); registering it across the PowerShell/Python config registry is a separate optional change.
